messages:
morgan: Quick hit — ran an eigenspectrum sweep across Mistral-7B, Mixtral-8x, Llama-2-13B and Qwen-14 to see how RoPE scaling (linear / NTK / YARN) influences kernel selection and batching behavior. attaching a tiny profiler excerpt below.

rahul: SGTM. Which sequence lengths?

morgan: 1) short (512) 2) mid (4096) 3) long (32k). Focus was on longctx perf and tail latency.

anya: curious if KV cache eviction patterns changed — did you keep continuous-batching on?

morgan: yes, continuous-batching on for all runs. Observations: 
- NTK variant shifts eigenmodes so head/kv dim alignment differs -> CUDA kernel chooser prefers fp16 matmul kernel for Mixtral, but Llama2 stayed on the slower generic matmul path.
- For Qwen the YARN variant produces a tighter eigenspectrum, higher prefix similarity -> KV hitrate up ~6% on longctx but batcher saw increased variance which bumped p99 by ~40ms.

lee: can you paste the profiler snippet?

morgan: here — trimmed: 
```
Model: mixtral-8x | seq=32768 | variant=NTK
kernel_choice: matmul_fp16_opt (60%), matmul_generic (25%), attention_kernel_fused (15%)
token_time_ms: median=12.3 p95=22.1 p99=45.8
KV_cache_hit_rate: 82.1%
batch_size_mean: 4.1 batch_var: 1.8
```

morgan: and for mistral-7b linear variant: 
```
Model: mistral-7b | seq=32768 | variant=Linear
kernel_choice: matmul_generic (55%), matmul_fp16_opt (30%), attention_kernel_fused (15%)
token_time_ms: median=14.9 p95=28.6 p99=63.4
KV_cache_hit_rate: 74.3%
batch_size_mean: 6.8 batch_var: 0.9
```

rahul: interesting — so Mixtral+NTK both improves kernel selection and KV hitrate, but batching variance causes p99 spike. That smells like the batcher heuristic (time-window vs max-window) interacting with prefix similarity.

anya: did you try forcing batching policy to max_items only?

morgan: yes — forcing max_items reduced batch variance and lowered p99 by ~30% on Mixtral, but token median slightly increased (sacrifice throughput). For Mistral linear, max_items made little diff.

lee: any perplexity/quality regressions from NTK vs linear?

morgan: ran eval sets — small perplexity blips for mixtral NTK at very long context (spike ~0.7 ppl) for a handful of samples where RoPE phase wraps. Not catastrophic but flags for safety range.

ops-bot: Incident check: no ongoing incidents tied to this perf test. :white_check_mark:

rahul: proposal: add eigenspectrum check in model onboarding that suggests kernel profile and default batching policy. heuristics: 
- If eigenspectrum tail energy ratio < 0.02 -> prefer NTK and set batcher=max_items with tight time-window
- If head/kv misalignment > 10% (head_dim vs kv_dim ratio) -> fallback to smaller batch sizes
- For Qwen-like tight spectra -> allow more aggressive prefix caching and larger batch windows but monitor p99

anya: +1. Also record a small regression test: run 1k prefix sequences at 16k/32k seq for each variant and assert p99 < baseline*1.5 and ppl delta < 1.0 on eval set.

morgan: will add a CI job and a lightweight profiler to output: eigenspectrum summary, chosen kernel histogram, KV hitrate, batch variance, p95/p99. attaching the first draft of the script in the PR.

lee: can you surface a per-model "safe range" doc? e.g., Mixtral-8x: NTK safe up to 48k with max_items batcher; Mistral-7B: linear safe up to 24k; Qwen-14: YARN recommended with conservative batching.

morgan: yep — I'll populate a per-model table and drop it in the onboarding repo. tagging @rahul for review. :rocket:

rahul: thanks — would also like a watch alert if kernel selection switches from fp16_opt -> generic on >5% of tokens for any model-release.

morgan: noted, will add alert and PR.

lee: nice work. short follow-up: can you include a tiny trace that maps attention kernel latency vs kv cache hit windows? that helped us previously.

morgan: will include, planning to run that tomorrow morning and post results. :calendar:
